summary: Embedded Semantic OS ontology and generated COY catalog namespaces now fail closed on malformed, partial, duplicated, out-of-order, or checksum-inconsistent markers while genuinely marker-free custom card documents retain local fallback.
decisions: Treat any ontology begin-prefix, end marker, or typed-fence sentinel as namespace presence and require exactly one correctly formed instance of each before parsing or stripping.
Reject non-hex and short ontology checksum tokens before the loader can interpret the embedded graph as absent and rebuild from visible cards.
Treat any catalog begin-prefix or end marker as namespace presence, require exactly one correctly formed pair, and bind the catalog marker digest to the checksum-verified embedded ontology payload.
Allow a catalog-free document with a valid embedded ontology and a fully marker-free custom card document, but reject a catalog namespace that has no embedded ontology authority.

Validate and replace the existing catalog before replacing the ontology during sync so an internally consistent old snapshot can advance to a new source payload while corrupt marker metadata still fails closed.
Keep catalog table-body exactness in the deterministic sync/check contract; marker validity and marker-to-payload identity are parser invariants.

gate_results.evidence: 34 passed, including malformed/partial ontology and catalog namespaces, catalog-to-payload checksum mismatch, marker-free fallback, ontology-without-catalog, catalog-without-ontology, duplicate prevention, and old-to-new source sync.

risks: Namespace detection is intentionally strict: literal ontology or catalog marker syntax in unrelated prose is treated as corruption rather than ignored.
Catalog table-body edits are detected by sync --check rather than by parse; its marker digest identifies the embedded ontology payload from which the table must be regenerated.
